entities.summary: Sophia Goudstikker was a Dutch-born German photographer and feminist pioneer. She was one of the premier women's rights activists in Munich at the turn of the century and a business partner and companion of Anita Augspurg. When their partnership dissolved, Goudstikker became a more moderate feminist and partnered with Ika Freudenberg. Goudstikker was the inspiration for three different writers' depictions of a more masculine woman, who defied typical feminine characterizations. She was the first unmarried German woman to obtain a royal license for photography and the first German woman allowed to argue cases before the youth court.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Sophia Goudstikker was a pioneering feminist and photographer who broke ground as the first unmarried German woman to obtain a royal license for photography. Her work also paved the way for future generations of women in photography.
